title: Developing grnland
text: model list class, fields: genes, n_genes, traits (indices selected genes), loci (data frame one row per evolvable parameter: name, code/param, , j) x0 (default starting expression state). grn() parses edges regulation matrix (parse_regulation()), expands evolvable loci (hill_loci()), resolves traits.

title: Developing grnland
text: develop() S3 generic returning list(X, status): full expression state every individual status code (0 ok, 1 convergence, 2 unstable, 3 non-finite). Hill networks, hill_develop_cpp() takes base parameters, locus table, genotype matrix starting states, individual: writes genotype network parameters (apply_genotype()); integrates ODE adaptive Dormand–Prince 5(4) right-hand side small (1e-5); polishes steady state Newton’s method tol. accepts result non-negative stays near integrated state, jump another branch. Otherwise integrates , tol; checks stability eigenvalues Jacobian. Starting states matter multistable networks (e.g. motif 5): simulations every offspring starts development parent’s state, populations stay branch unless mutation pushes .

title: Developing grnland
text: hill_derivs_cpp() returns right-hand side f, Jacobian J df/dp every locus, analytical. , sensitivity(): S = dx*/dp = -J^{-1} df/dp (implicit function theorem); m_matrix(): M = S_T Σ S_T', S_T holds rows trait genes Σ = ploidy · μ · diag(σ²); genotype_at(): inverts map. loci exactly alphas, steady-state equations linear alpha solved directly; otherwise runs Newton’s method loci using S. Custom models use user’s Jacobian given, otherwise finite differences.

title: Developing grnland
text: landscape function n × d phenotype matrix n fitness values, class grn_landscape attributes n_dim info. attribute n_dim dim, structure() refuses set dim function. landscape_grid() precomputes 2D landscape interpolates bilinearly. Perlin noise matters: ambient large fixed cost per call, caching makes simulations three times faster. find_peaks() scans grid 2D, merging maxima closer merge cells. stops flat tops producing duplicate peaks. dimensions runs multistart optim(). Perlin noise ambient exactly flat along x within lattice cells, lines y · frequency = k + ½. Expect degenerate critical points . lande_separatrices() ignores points domain edge.

title: Developing grnland
text: State: alleles (N × L × ploidy; diploids copy carries half starting value), expression X (N × n_genes), fitness W, flag individuals whose development failed. generation: Selection. selection(W) turns fitness sampling weights. default selection_relative_min() original scripts’ w - min(w) + 0.001. Reproduction. Clonal reproduction resamples individuals. Sexual reproduction samples mothers fathers (separate halves sexes = TRUE) builds gametes free recombination. Mutation. Draws number mutations Binomial(N·L·ploidy, μ), adds Normal(0, σ) effects, clamps alleles [lower, upper]. Development. individuals whose genotype changed developed , starting parent’s expression state. Failed developments lethal (fitness NA, weight 0) , invalid = "reject", mutation undone. Recording stopping. Every record_every generations stores means, phenotypic covariance optionally M mean genotype. Every stop$every generations stopping rule checked. cost dominated development changed individuals landscape evaluation. paper’s settings generation takes 1 ms cached landscape.

title: Developing grnland
text: deterministic evolution dz/dt = G ∇W, G ∝ M(z) (fixed G), works follows: 1. Evaluate landscape grid take finite-difference gradients Hessians. 2. Find critical points Newton’s method lattice seeds, keep non-degenerate saddles. 3. Trace stable manifold saddle backwards RK4. G positive definite, critical points types landscape.

title: Developing grnland
text: new locus type Hill networks (e.g. basal-expression term): 1. Add parameter dynamics rhs() jac() hill.cpp. 2. Give new code apply_genotype() derivative dfdp(). 3. Handle new class name hill_loci(). 4. Add finite-difference test sensitivity(). new model class: 1. Write constructor returning fields listed Models. 2. Write develop.<class>() method. 3. sensitivity(), genotype_at() default_genotype() can’t use generic code, add branches class. Everything downstream, including m_matrix() simulate_population(), works unchanged. new landscape: wrap function landscape_function(f, dim), write constructor calls new_landscape(). new selection scheme stopping rule: selection scheme function fitness weights. stopping rule list every fun(X) -> peak index NULL. See stop_at_peaks().

title: Getting started with grnland
text: Networks written edges: "-> b" means activates b, "-| b" means represses b. gene follows Hill-type kinetics, \[\dot x_i = \alpha_i \prod_j H_{ij}(x_j) - \gamma_i x_i,\] production rate \(\alpha_i\), decay rate \(\gamma_i\), \(H_{ij}(x) = x^h/(\theta^h + x^h)\) activation, \(1 - x^h/(\theta^h + x^h)\) repression. parameter can locus: whole classes ("alpha", "gamma", "theta", "hill") single entries ("alpha[b]", "theta[c,]"). Genes listed traits still develop regulate, invisible selection. six two-gene motifs paper built :
code: m <- grn(c("a -> b", "b -| c", "c -> a", "a -| c"),          alpha = c(4, 6, 8), theta = 3,          evolvable = c("alpha", "theta"),  # parameters that mutate          traits = c("b", "c"))             # genes under selection m #> <hill_grn> 3 genes, 7 loci, traits: b, c #> edges: a -> b, a -| c, b -| c, c -> a  #> loci: alpha[a], alpha[b], alpha[c], theta[a,c], theta[b,a], theta[c,a], theta[c,b] paper_motif(3)   # x1 -> x2, x2 -| x1 #> <hill_grn> 2 genes, 2 loci, traits: x1, x2 #> edges: x1 -> x2, x2 -| x1  #> loci: alpha[x1], alpha[x2]

title: Getting started with grnland
text: genotype_at() goes way, finding genotype develops target phenotype:
code: g <- default_genotype(m) g #> [1] 4 6 8 3 3 3 3 phenotype(m, g)          # steady state of the trait genes #>        b        c  #> 2.335530 2.747221 develop(m, g)$status     # 0 = converged to a stable steady state #> [1] 0 mot <- paper_motif(5) g5 <- genotype_at(mot, c(2, 6)) phenotype(mot, g5) #> x1 x2  #>  2  6

title: Getting started with grnland
text: sensitivity matrix \(S = \partial x^*/\partial p\) computed analytically Jacobian dynamics (\(S = -J^{-1}\,\partial f/\partial p\)). per-locus mutation rate \(\mu\) mutational effect \(\sigma\), M-matrix \(M = S\,\Sigma\,S^\top\) \(\Sigma = \mu\sigma^2 \) (times ploidy). phenotype differently shaped M motif. six paper motifs one phenotype, scaled unit trace:
code: m_matrix(mot, phenotype = c(2, 6), mu = 0.01, sigma = 0.05) #>              x1           x2 #> x1 1.641190e-05 3.562623e-05 #> x2 3.562623e-05 7.936391e-05 library(ggplot2) ellipse <- function(M, n = 100) {   e <- eigen(M / sum(diag(M)), symmetric = TRUE)   t <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n)   pts <- cbind(cos(t), sin(t)) %*% diag(sqrt(pmax(e$values, 0))) %*% t(e$vectors)   data.frame(x = pts[, 1], y = pts[, 2]) } shapes <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:6, function(k)   cbind(ellipse(m_matrix(paper_motif(k), phenotype = c(3, 3))), motif = paste("motif", k)))) ggplot(shapes, aes(x, y)) + geom_polygon(fill = "steelblue", colour = "black") +   facet_wrap(~motif, nrow = 1) + coord_equal() + theme_void()

title: Getting started with grnland
text: trajectory records mean phenotype, phenotypic covariance matrix (P_*), mean fitness number individuals whose development failed. Set record_m = TRUE also record M-matrix mean genotype. Options include: ploidy = 2, reproduction = "sexual" diploid sexual populations free recombination (sexes = TRUE separate sexes); selection = selection_proportional() selection_exponential(s) instead default original scripts (w - min(w) + 0.001); invalid = "reject" resample offspring whose development fails instead treating lethal; stop = stop_at_peaks(peaks) stop population sits peak.

title: Getting started with grnland
text: Even single symmetric peak, network shapes path. six motifs start phenotype climb peak:  Motifs whose M positive covariance traits (1, 3, 5) first move left, along long axis M, fitness rises fastest variation , turn towards peak. Motifs negative covariance (2, 4) head right, unregulated motif 6 takes direct route. rugged landscapes differences can decide peak reached: see article Paper figures examples.
code: paths <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:6, function(k) {   s <- simulate_population(paper_motif(k), land, start = c(2, 6), N = 500,                            generations = 3000, record_every = 10, seed = k,                            stop = stop_at_peaks(matrix(c(5, 3), 1)))   cbind(s$trajectory[, c("generation", "mean_x1", "mean_x2")], motif = paste("motif", k)) })) bg <- expand.grid(x1 = seq(0, 7, length.out = 150), x2 = seq(1, 7, length.out = 150)) bg$w <- land(as.matrix(bg)) ggplot(bg, aes(x1, x2)) + geom_raster(aes(fill = w)) +   scale_fill_gradient(low = "grey20", high = "grey95", name = "fitness") +   geom_path(data = paths, aes(mean_x1, mean_x2, colour = motif), linewidth = 0.9) +   annotate("point", 2, 6, shape = 21, size = 3, fill = "white") +   coord_equal(expand = FALSE) + labs(x = expression(x[1]), y = expression(x[2]))

title: Paper figures and examples
text: Script: motif_example.R. paper figures, single-picture example main idea. six motifs start phenotype (2, 12) rugged landscape (Perlin frequency 0.3, seed 4). M-matrices point different directions (panel B), climb three different peaks (panels C), 10 diploid sexual replicates per motif reach peak predicted deterministic Lande flow \(\dot{\bar z} = M\nabla W\).  Motifs positive covariance traits (1, 3, 5) go peak , negative covariance (2, 4) peak C, unregulated motif 6, isotropic M-matrix, peak B.

title: Paper figures and examples
text: Script: fig1_linear_maps.R. linear map \(x = B\alpha\) diploid M-matrix constant, \(M = 2\mu\sigma^2 BB^\top\). Three equal-determinant maps (covariance, positive, negative; unbounded alleles) evolve single Gaussian peak () two-peak Perlin landscape (B–D; frequency 0.15, seed 96, offset (0, -2.5), \(31 \times 31\) grid, 10 replicates per start). Outcomes classified SVM (red border \(\mathbf{B}_1\), white borders \(\mathbf{B}_2, \mathbf{B}_3\); 10-fold CV accuracies 99.6%, 99.0%, 99.1%) compared deterministic Lande separatrix (dashed black).
code: B <- list(B1 = diag(2),           B2 = matrix(c(5, 4, 4, 5) / 3, 2),           B3 = matrix(c(5, -4, -4, 5) / 3, 2)) models <- lapply(B, gp_linear) land <- landscape_perlin(frequency = 0.15, seed = 96, offset = c(0, -2.5)) lande <- lande_separatrices(models$B2, land, lower = -2, upper = 12)

text: genes \(= 1..n\), \[\dot x_i = \alpha_i \prod_j H_{ij}(x_j) - \gamma_i x_i,\] \(H_{ij}(x) = x^h/(\theta^h + x^h)\) gene \(j\) activates gene \(\), \(1 - x^h/(\theta^h + x^h)\) \(j\) represses \(\), 1 don’t interact (\(\theta = \theta_{ij}\), \(h = h_{ij}\)). phenotype steady state development reaches. regulation can also matrix regulation[, j] effect gene j gene (+1, -1 0). evolvable accepts whole parameter classes ("alpha", "gamma", "theta", "hill") single entries ("alpha[b]", "theta[c,]"). six motifs paper available paper_motif(1) paper_motif(6).

title: grnland: evolution of gene regulatory networks on adaptive landscapes
text: defaults reproduce settings paper’s scripts: haploid clonal populations 1000, per-locus mutation rate 0.01, mutational sd 0.05, alleles truncated 0, w - min(w) + 0.001 selection weights “half population within ±0.1 peak” convergence rule. inst/examples/grid_screen.R shows full grid screen starting points.
code: land <- landscape_grid(landscape_perlin(frequency = 0.5, seed = 1245)) peaks <- find_peaks(land, 0, 15) sim <- simulate_population(   paper_motif(1), land, start = c(4, 6),   N = 1000, generations = 10000, mu = 0.01, sigma = 0.05,   ploidy = 1, reproduction = "clonal",          # or ploidy = 2, "sexual"   selection = selection_relative_min(),         # or selection_proportional(), selection_exponential(s)   stop = stop_at_peaks(peaks), record_m = TRUE, seed = 1) sim$outcome       # index of the peak reached (NA if none) sim$trajectory    # means, phenotypic (co)variances P_*, M_*, mean fitness per recorded generation

what: Differences from the original analysis scripts
title: grnland: evolution of gene regulatory networks on adaptive landscapes
text: Steady states computed numerically every network, closed forms. six motifs agree closed forms 1e-8, sensitivities agree analytical expressions Fig2.r (see tests/testthat/test-motifs.R). Motif 5 (mutual activation): \(\alpha_1\alpha_2 < \theta^2\) network goes zero state, dynamics ; closed form gives negative expression . stale-phenotype bug Fig5.r exist : phenotypes always recomputed mutated genotype. Individuals whose development fails (stable steady state) get zero fitness default (invalid = "lethal"); invalid = "reject" discards offending mutation instead. Random numbers drawn differently, runs reproduce paper’s results statistically, draw draw.
